subject: installing rapache on mac osx - problems with apxs and make

messages.author: a246b4ab95a97093
messages.subject: installing rapache on mac osx - problems with apxs and make
parts:
Hi everyone


I am trying to install rapache on my mac to give my users a front end to generate plots using ggplo2.

I am trying to install from source using the following commands

./configure --with-R=/usr/bin/r --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/sbin/apxs

as in my machine apxs is located at /usr/sbin/apxs

I noticed that during this command, I get the following output

checking for apxs2... checking for R Program... /usr/bin/r
checking for apreq2-config... no

and then the 'make' command fails

env: /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/OSX10.8.xctoolchain/usr/bin/cc: No such file or directory
apxs:Error: Command failed with rc=65536

Is there something I am doing wrong here?

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks.
SN

messages.author: b2a4f8328faaf97f
messages.subject: Re: installing rapache on mac osx - problems with apxs and make
parts:
Hi SN,
there is one step in the README that you missed, that is probably causing your problems. You have to install librareq2 before installing rApache, and then later give ./configure the location to the apreq2-config in an additional flag when installing rApache afterwards as so:
    --with-apreq2-config=/path/to/apreq2-config
You have to install it manually from the folder /libapreq2 in the rApache-1.2.3 folder that you got when you unzipped your rApache download, there is another README for it.

The fact that your env variable gave that error might be because you probably have only the command-line version of Xcode installed, or do not have it installed at all. In the first case, i recommend installing the full version and slimming it down later, as the CLI-version has numerous shortcomings and will cause problems again and again. Sadly, OSX does not seem to care about some major bugs in it that you will find people complaining about on Stackoverflow again and again.
In the second case, you should know that you need to have Xcode installed for the installation to work.

Best regards,
Z
